title: Token escape handling and template heuristics for model pinning
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem:
During recent model onboarding runs we observed intermittent chat-template rendering errors and small but measurable token-count variance after pinning to model revisions with different tokenizer metadata. Root causes identified: inconsistent escape/whitespace handling across tokenizer manifests, delimiter collisions between template role markers and model-specific special tokens, and heuristics in the template renderer that assume single-byte separators.

Goal:
Make tokenizer + chat-template handling resilient for pinned model revisions and ensure we publish an accurate performance profile when tokenizer mapping deviates from our canonical assumptions. Provide a compatibility shim at onboarding time that either normalizes templates or flags required template updates.

Proposed solution summary:
1) Tokenizer normalization layer at onboarding: canonicalize whitespace, normalize common escape sequences (e.g., NBSP, zero-width), and produce a token-boundary map that the renderer can consume.
2) Template heuristic updates: when a pinned model introduces tokens that collide with system role delimiters (e.g., "<assistant>", "<|end|>"), apply a deterministic escaping strategy or suggest an alternate delimiter to the PM/Design owner and record the chosen mapping in model metadata.
3) Compatibility shim & warning surface: compute a tokenizer-compatibility score during onboarding. If score < threshold, mark the model as "template-adjustment-recommended" and attach a short, auto-generated migration note for SDKs and Console.
4) Performance profile publishing: when tokenizer normalization alters expected token counts by >3% for representative prompts, publish a separate performance profile (e.g., runtime-2.3/tokenizer-adjusted) that includes the observed per-token throughput and latency breakdown.

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarding pipeline emits a compatibility report JSON and a human-readable migration note for low-score models.
- Unit tests cover boundary cases: surrogate pairs, combining marks, NBSP, zero-width joiners, repeated delimiter tokens.
- Integration test against a pinned model revision replicates the earlier failure and verifies the shim prevents template rendering errors.
- If performance delta >3% is detected, a secondary performance profile is produced and visible in the Console under the model's Performance tab.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Large-scale rework of all chat templates across customers.
- Changes to public SDK APIs beyond adding a compatibility warning field in model metadata.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Initial triage complete. Reproduced template rendering error with pinned rev r12 using test harness. Failure triggered by tokenizer returning '\u00A0' as separate token causing the renderer to treat it as role delimiter. Added repro snippet to drive (link below).

2026-03-03 - Diego Morales: Implemented a prototype normalization pass that replaces NBSP and zero-width characters with normalized spaces before tokenization. Early CI shows reduction in token variance for the repro set (mean delta down from 5.1% to 1.2%).
2026-03-05 - Maya Patel (code review): Please add explicit tests for emoji sequences and ZWJ sequences. Also request logging on the compatibility score so PM can evaluate sensitivity.

2026-03-06 - Diego Morales: Added tests for emoji/ZWJ combos and expanded compatibility scoring to include delimiter collision detection. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8427
2026-03-08 - Liam Park (PM): Migration note wording is important for UX. Suggested phrasing and examples added to the PR description. Confirming Console should show a red flag if score < 0.6.

2026-03-09 - CI: Integration test 'pinned-model-template-repro' failed on macOS runner with unexpected token count +4. Investigation points to a tokenizer variant that encodes '»' as two subtokens. Added diagnostic logging.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Fixed variant mapping bug by normalizing delimiter escapes before invoking the tokenizer shim. Re-ran integration tests: all green. Preparing for canary rollout to 10% of new onboardings next week.
rollout_plan: Canary: 10% of new model onboardings for 72 hours; monitor compatibility_score and perf delta. If false positives exceed 2/day, rollback the shim and open follow-up ticket for expanded token-vector heuristics.
